title: Technical decisions that are product decisions wearing a disguise

videos.script: At Coreto, a seat is held while the buyer pays. How long that hold lasts is one number in a configuration file. {{hold}} Mateus's team wanted to shorten it, because long holds pile up in the database when a big show goes on sale. It looked like a performance fix. It is also a decision about which buyers lose their seats. {{buyers}} Make the hold shorter, and somebody typing a card number loses the seat before paying. Make it longer, and the show looks sold out while seats sit with people who walked away. Neither answer is wrong in engineering terms. Choosing between them is a product decision. {{product}} This lesson is about decisions like that one. They arrive in technical words, a cache lifetime, a retention period, an availability target, a door scanner with no network. {{disguise}} You will learn the marks that give them away. And you will learn to put them in front of product as options, each with its consequences, so the person who owns the outcome can choose. {{options}}
